notes.title: Kingdom-Crier #11: Love and Elves has Released!
notes.notes:
Hey hey, the time has finally come!

Feature Update #3 has been released!

[h1]Love and Elves![/h1]
[h3]Noble Fates Feature Update #3[/h3]

Elves have come to Noberia from far away lands, bringing the custom of Marriage with them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/00af14a347c2d6095afd870a273742c5452c097f.png[/img]

Can you find the perfect partners for your people?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/036f4d3bd78d58b0082b0e4f433a64b7c0fad5e5.png[/img]

[h2]Elves![/h2]
A patient Race - Elves live twice as long as Humans and Orcs, but take their time maturing - progressing at half the rate of the other Races.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/edda91398175d16aa1ad0d6efde24adceaf8d221.png[/img]

Elves don't mind Humans, but can be at odds with the Orcs!

Elves have increased potential in Hunting and Crafting, though their smaller frame limits their potential in Melee.

[h2]Updated Characters![/h2]
To ensure the adoption of Marriage across the lands, the Gods have blessed the other Mortal Races with new faces, haircuts, and finally... Ears!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/752f374878909616ce91bc725d8125d239017278.png[/img]

Enjoy new Human and Orc faces with many more variation and much more detail than before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/481af4c1b7cf28fc1da66d447563270d4200a2bd.png[/img]

[h2]Attraction![/h2]
Now that the Mortals are more beautiful, they've discovered that they're now Attracted to one another!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/cbb404dacdd9f395cdb0a970c671cfe7e5f03179.png[/img]

Browse the new Attraction tab on the Character Sheet to see what each Mortal is into.

Mortals have a broad range of preferences - taking Gender, Age, Race, and even wealth into account when sizing up a potential partner.

[h2]Gifts![/h2]
The Mortals have discovered that they can grow and harvest Flowers, making Bouquets for gifts to maximize their chances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/7173347bc3de08ce2ec583fe8365af59affc7240.png[/img]

Daily gifts can help that friendship blossom into true Love!

Use the additional details on the expanded Relationship tab to see just why two Mortals love one-another or why they aren't getting along.

[h2]Marriage![/h2]
Build and decorate the new Wedding Arch to arrange a Wedding between two of your Mortals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/1d24ba14f6c3124b42f4845832ba66dcbd3185fb.png[/img]

Marry an Enamored pair of Mortals to transform their shared Love into Loyalty or arrange a one-sided Marriage to keep an important Noble happy!

Interactions with a Mortal's partner have increased effects on that Mortal - treat your Mortal's partners well to keep them happy.

Leverage Double Beds and shared Lodgings to simplify housing for your growing Kingdom!
 
Marriages last until one of the partners dies, so make sure you make the right call when choosing a Mortal's partner!

[h2]Expanded Intro Details and Options![/h2]
This was the perfect time to increase the information shared during the Intro and we've coupled that with the introduction of per-Mortal Reroll support.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/ade40d75eed31556b5c00e7e0cb0ce4fabb0c5f8.png[/img]

We plan to do more with the Intro as we move further into EA, but this should help those of you looking for that perfect group from the start.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/172199ccfb9aee15c6f681108c4939f63829db7d.png[/img]

[h2]Other Surprises[/h2]
Beyond Elves, we've also added Innate abilities to the other Races - Orcs have higher potential in Melee and Mining, but lower in Hunting; Humans have increased Building and Farming but aren't as capable in Foraging.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/5a755be808d062391244cf9b1fe6b10a12e8af3d.png[/img]

In addition, we introduced Skirts and Blouses - a slightly nicer variant of Tunics and Leggings that can roll brighter colors - perfect for a Wedding!

The Experimental Beta included Top Hats and Veils - but we've expanded both to include a wider array of colors.

Finally - we've introduced new Breach Music - fitting music for a fitting end for a Kingdom.

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
Leverage the new Caps Visibility toggle to let those luscious locks loose.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/c51cb79212445a753f68d3f249123866252089be.png[/img]

We retuned Depth of Field to better accommodate close-ups of your new faces.

We rebalanced Kingdom Size preference - more Mortals than ever will prefer Medium or Large Kingdoms.

Finally, we optimized startup time! Even with the added burden of the new Character Art, the game should load faster and use less memory than ever before!

[h3]Saves[/h3]
These changes necessitated changes to the save game format, so this update retires 0.25 saves.

We've spun up a retired_0_25 set of Steam Betas so that you can continue your 0.25 saves there or go back and visit them whenever you want.

[h3]Full Changelist[/h3]

notes.title: Kingdom-Crier #9: Performance, Performance, Performance!
notes.notes:
Hey hey - Welcome to Kingdom-Crier #9!

[h1]Performance[/h1]
As you know, we've been focused on performance for the last two weeks. Here's a rundown of what we were able to accomplish.

[h2]Patch #1: Rendering[/h2]
As we detailed in the last Crier, the Render Thread was a central source of performance problems for medium to large size bases - often doubling the length of time of the Main Thread. This was primarily due to the interaction between Unity's approach to parallel rendering and our use of common materials which increased the per-object type draw call count.

At the end of the day, Unity can handle around 2k draw calls if you still want to hit 30fps on an average machine. We had several things at play that caused these numbers to balloon for us - although we used instancing to draw the instances of a given object together, each separate material type/color on an object would generate a separate draw call for them. In addition, stacked items on the ground would generate one for each stack size. 

The optimization here combined these per material and per mesh by doing a little bit of baking work on startup. This means that we can draw hundreds of stacks of a given item type of various sizes with one draw call now! In addition, we were able to flip some optimization flags on our textures to save system memory at the same time - so there should be less pressure on that precious RAM.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/b3cc38beb22ce003b5e5a3fc09b6f1fab448ce9e.png[/img]

[h2]Patch #2: Animals[/h2]
This one is kind of funny. Once Render Thread pressure was dialed back a bit, we switched focus back to the Main Thread, where it was clear that we were spending too much time updating characters. In some of the worst saves, this would add up to 100ms or more!

Whenever a visiting party with animals was disbanded, their animals would be turned loose in the local area. Animals in Noble Fates hadn't yet evolved the ability to die of old age or starve and without any predators this meant they'd just kind of stick around forever.

We've introduced two things to help address this. First, animal migration. When the local population of a given animal type is too high, a subset of the wild animals of that type will move on to greener pastures. They'll make their way to the edge of the map and find a new home with less local contention. Second, animals can now starve. Beyond increasing the reality of the simulation - at least once we get it dialed in - this should help introduce a bit more ebb and flow in the local wildlife population as well as increasing the difficulty of maintaining large ranches.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/b16903093cfe0e6f28636abadd9491ac9eddb987.png[/img]

This was primarily an issue in late-game saves, where we've seen as many as 1000(!) animals when there should be less than 100.

[h2]Patch #3: Characters[/h2]
Characters continued to stick out as expensive once we resolved the animal population issues, so we turned our attention to the simulation. There are a number of complex queries that characters run.

They would examine all of the kingdom's items when evaluating their equipment, all props when looking for a warm fire to sit by, and everything on the map when deciding what to eat or drink. This runs fine at small scale bases - and can even hold up for mid-scale bases on good machines, but once you've got a few thousand items laying around or a few thousand props, these become very expensive.

To reduce this strain, we introduced additional constraints on the queries that can be performed, using additional information like item type, prop type, or region to greatly reduce the search space when making these decisions.

We also found and fixed a nasty bug that caused slowdown when placing props - it should be smoother than ever now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/03d85c7db5157d3b500481b58b400b3858eddb66.png[/img]

[i]Noble Fates 0.25.0.49 Patch Notes[/i]
[code]Crash Fixes
    Fix for crash related to perception

Performance
    Improve Prop Placing Performance
    Improve Item performance
        Amortize Update Cost
    Improve Prop performance
        Improve Search Cost
    Improve Character performance
        Amortize Update Cost
        Reduce cost of Finding a Spot to Relax
        Reduce cost of Finding a Prop to Attack
        Reduce cost of Searching for Food
        Reduce cost of Searching for Materials
        Reduce cost of Searching for Training Dummy
        Reduce cost of Evaluating Equipment
    Paused
        Reduce unnecessary work when Paused

Research
    Fix bug that caused characters to idle instead of Researching Dependencies
    
Combat
    Improve AI behavior when switching targets
    Fix bug that caused Imps to hold aggro on people leaving the map
    
Relaxing
    Improve seat usage near Heat Sources
    
Portraits
    Update Portraits as needed occasionally when Live Portraits are disabled
    
Animals
    Double food received from grazing[/code]
[h2]Results[/h2]
The Rendering pass provided the biggest bump, raising our Average framerate 30% across our tests. This is most noticeable during pause, slow, and 1x gameplay. Next, the Character pass raised the average framerate by 25% across a variety of mid to late games. This is most noticeable at 1x and above, but especially at 10x speeds. Finally, the Animal patch helped late-games a fair bit - providing a 21% boost across the board - but it was generally all or nothing showing up as no gain if you didn't have an animal population problem, and up to a 100% gain if you did!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/d4a89e5e7ca381e089ac1722741393e46a77897b.png[/img]

Overall, framerate increased an average of [b]86%[/b] across our tests - raising the average [b]late-game[/b] frame rate from under 15fps to [b]28fps[/b]. Not bad!

[h2]The Future[/h2]
Things are in a decent spot for now - especially relative to where we started - so we're shifting focus back to the next Feature Update. There are a number of optimizations remaining that we plan to do - those animated portraits are expensive, culling stuff on other layers would be a big win, and there's more to do with the simulation.

Some of these are small enough that we can pick them up as smaller patches, and it's likely that we do one or two more of these Performance specific sprints in the future.

[h1]What's new in Main?[/h1]
We've been focused almost exclusively on performance, but a few other changes snuck in:

[code]We resolved an issue that prevented variation in Combat rate!
We added support for other animal product types - check out KRanching![/code]

Thanks for reading and thanks for playing!

[h1]Content Updates[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/58e64f136524d158bfcf8b72cbfedb134bfcc8ff.png[/img]

[h1]Performance[/h1]
Let's talk about performance.

Noble Fates is complex. The world sim is single threaded and runs on the main CPU thread. This handles all of the interactions in your kingdom, storage and command scheduling, and all of the background interactions in the world. The rendering system uses Unity's graphics jobs system - but really it's largely constrained to a second single CPU thread, the render thread, which dispatches the jobs to the other cores for processing during a brief period of time.

Once the main CPU thread is done simulating, it turns the render thread loose to draw everything while it helps where it can for half a frame or so. Once it's done helping, it can move on to the next frame's simulation. This means that rendering can run in parallel to the simulation when things are going well.

Generally speaking, to run at 30fps, your sim needs to take less than 16ms and your render thread work needs to take less than 33ms. Overages on either of these can result in low utilization of your CPU even though we're CPU bound - with the main thread waiting for the render thread to finish the last frame or the render thread is waiting for the main thread so it can start rendering the next frame. VSync can exasperate this problem further by adding an additional wait on the main thread where it synchronizes with your GPU before starting the next simulation step.

As your game progresses and you add more people and build out your base, it stresses both of these threads in different ways, and ultimately increases the likelihood that one or both of them runs over-time and the other is left waiting.  In extreme cases, you can end up with your sim taking 50ms and the rendering taking 150ms which resulting in a ~150ms frame time or 6fps even though most of your CPU is waiting for work.

We've previously done a lot of optimization work on the sim, and it's generally in an okay place. The big problem at the moment is render thread performance. We have some work in progress that shows lots of promise here, but it needs some focused time to wrap it up. Based on early tests, it should do as much as double our framerate in these situations!

Given where we're at, with a decently stable early game and more and more of you driving into the mid/late game, we think it's best to attack this issue and increase the breadth of what the game can handle to set us up for the next phase of Early Access. 

[b]To that end, we're going to spend the next two weeks focused on performance.[/b]

Though it's well underway, this means that the next Feature Update is going to be announced 2 weeks later than usual (4 weeks from now instead of 2) - but we think it's worth it to focus our efforts here for a short while.

if you have any questions or concerns, feel free to leave them below!

Hail Kontras! Welcome to Kingdom-Crier #7!

[h1]UI Toggle[/h1]
We've heard your pleas for a way to take polished looking screenshots!

Fret no more, press [F9] to toggle the game's UI so you can take those sweet screenshots to show off your kingdom!

[h1]Screenshot Contest #1[/h1]
We're happy to announce our first Screenshot Contest!

Take a sweet new screenshot of the game and post it to #kingdom-shots on our Official [url=https://discord.gg/HeAaQcS]Discord[/url] to enter. First Place will receive $50 USD, Second: $25 USD, and Third: $10 USD. The contest runs through 5/1 at 11:59 PST.

notes.title: Crier #6: The Bandit Update and Steam Workshop Now Available!
notes.notes:
The Bandit Update is here!

The Noble Fates Steam Workshop is now available!!

To celebrate, Noble Fates is on sale for 20% off for the next 2 weeks!

[previewyoutube=rDTmCqrxQjI;full][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/b0de5b9d8656eac429bc9a2d492623b9970c9d90.png[/img][/previewyoutube]
[h1]The Bandit Update![/h1]
[h3]Noble Fates Feature Update #2 has Released![/h3]
Some of the more nefarious Mortals have discovered that they can make a living in Noberia by robbing and stealing!

Keep them away from any loose belongings laying around. Give your visitors a safe place to sleep for the night so they aren't robbed blind.

Deal with the Bandits or they'll slap together a sketchy structure or eight on the edge of your lands to house all of their sweet loot.

Profit from their exploits or send them packing, it's your call!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/e12ce1be96d11f6aed6b95d8a92caf9e31aa7797.png[/img]

[h2]Quests![/h2]
Mortals accosted by Bandits can now ask for help through the new Quest system! See that little exclamation point above their heads? You know what to do. Decide if they're worthy of your time and choose how you want to handle their request.

Do you pay the Bandits to get the victim's stuff back, offer them something they deem of equal value in trade, or beat it out of them?!

Maybe you decide not to return that nice Crossbow of Ranging now that it's in your hands. The choice is yours, the consequences are part of the fun!

[h2]Ramshackle Props![/h2]
We couldn't give the Bandits new Props to build with without making them available for your sweet setups.

The starter building tier is now Ramshackle. They offer fast and cheap shelter, but aren't worth much and might just fall down at the slightest glance from an enemy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/cdd1c2b86061365fa430a2333cf9d3899e739db1.png[/img]

[h2]Steam Workshop![/h2]
We're excited to launch the Noble Fates Steam Workshop with this update. Browse and Subscribe to the mods you're interested in right inside of Steam!

Manage them in-game through the new Mod Management interface. Modders - Upload or Update your mods with ease using the in-game tools.

[h2]Surprise! Crossbows![/h2]
Enjoy a new type of Secondary Ranged Weapon!

Projectiles travel faster and straighter, but it takes longer to prepare that next shot!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/ea3021a8a1afb1a5ffd06aceeef070e31e0ec8e6.png[/img]

[h2]Steam Cloud Saves![/h2]
We hit the big flashing red button to enable Steam Cloud Saves with this update!

Your Kingdoms will be there and waiting for you at whatever PC you play at next.

[h2]Full Patch Notes[/h2]
[code]Noble Fates 0.25.0.15 (The Bandit Update!)

Expand NPC Factions
    Add support for planning buildings and settlements
    Add support for planning stockpiles
    Add support for NPC owned loose items
    Hide blueprints for NPC Factions
    Hide stockpiles for NPC factions
    Improve belonging abandonment when leaving the map
    
Bandits
    Parties can become Bandits
    Add Bandit Disguises
    Add support for taxing Bandits
    Add support for evicting Bandits
    Add support for buying out Bandits
    Prevent Bandits from buying food
    Prevent Bandits from renting rooms
    Prevent Bandits from helping with kingdom tasks
    
Crossbows
    A new type of Ranged Secondary Weapon
    Higher velocity projectiles than Short Bows
    Slower firing rate than Short Bows
        
Add Scheme System
    Allows NPC groups to organize into activities
    Add Build Scheme
    Add Rob Scheme
    Add Steal Scheme
    Add Forage Scheme
    Add Fight Schemes
    
Quests
    Add Quest system (called missions in code)
    Add support for Quest markers
    Add support for Quest conversations
    Add Recover Belongings Quest

Ramshackle Structural Props
    New tier of Structural Props
    Switch Guided Experience to Ramshackle Props
    Weaker than Wood tier
    Built faster than Wood tier
    Require less resources than Wood tier
    
Mods
    Add Mod Management Menu
    Add support for Steam Workshop
    Add support for ordering mods in-game
    
Save Games
    Track which Mods are used within a given save game
    Warn when loading with a different set of Mods loaded
    Enable Steam Cloud Saves
    
Justifications
    Expand justified killings to include Bandit Fight Schemes
    Expand justified imprisonment to include Bandits

Tools
    Improve building tool sorting
    Expand/contract tools list based on resolution and UI Scale
    
Perception
    Limit perception of Bandits
    Limit perception of retreating Attackers
    
Animal List
    Only show details for animals that a Kingdom Members has seen
    
Wood Structural Props
    Move research back a few levels
    
Stolen Goods
    Launder when possessor leaves the map
    Abandon when original owners leaves the map
    Automatically returned to owner if faction comes into possession
    
Items
    Add support for items being stolen
    Add support for items being referenced by quests
    
Trading Screen
    Reflect quest status of Items
    Reflect stolen status of items
    
Item Tooltips
    Add stolen info
    Add quest info
    
UX
    Escape will no longer exit the game from the Main Menu
    Escape will now close the Load Game list from the Main Menu
    
Memory
    Reduce memory usage by up to 1GB[/code]
[h3]Save Compatibility[/h3]
The Bandits were just too powerful to be boxed in by existing save limitations, so this update retires 0.24 saves.

We have spun up a retired_0_24 set of Steam Betas so that you can continue your 0.24 saves there or go back and visit them whenever you want.

[h2]Experimental Beta[/h2]
With the release of the update, we're retiring the Experimental Beta for now.

Your Experimental saves carry over now that this update has been released.

[h1]What's new in Main?[/h1]
We've been all in on this update and the Steam features, but there have been a few important fixes worth calling out:

We added Stone Stairs!

notes.title: Kingdom-Crier #4: Customization, Roadmap Update, and Straw!
notes.notes:
Welcome Kontras! This is Kingdom-Crier #4!

Herein you'll find info about the first bit of in-game Customization, updates to the roadmap, and today's new Content Update!

[h1]Customization[/h1]
Last week we tackled the first bit of Noble and Kingdom Customization, allowing you to rename your Nobles, re-title your Ruler, rename your Kingdom, and even rename your lands. We took it even further allowing you to rename anyone who visits (including their Kingdom and Lands) to allow you to make your world your own! This has been nicely integrated into the intro - making it more streamlined than before.

[i]Edit your Ruler and Kingdom during the Intro![/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/d946e10fed98019eaa57de7e5a732c7c5b33cf90.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/486de38b321fbae8c5ffc68616a79c1850fc3bd2.png[/img]

We plan to do more here, but this should help open up the options for expressing yourself in-game.

[h1]Roadmap Update[/h1]
With the customization above, we've wrapped up the initial wave of Hot Fixes that we've been tracking since launch!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/afe2a9d0a75363d8516d8d28f5c238e888d2be9d.png[/img]

notes.title: Kingdom-Crier #3: Key Binding, Longer Years, and Tavern Content!
notes.notes:
Greetings Kontras! Welcome to Kingdom-Crier #3!

Exciting things to report in this Crier as we addressed one of the largest outstanding QOL issues with Key Binding, we extended the time you get with your Mortals via Longer Years, and we added Content Update #6 to help finish off those Taverns.

[h1]Key Binding[/h1]
Key Binding has been added to Noble Fates! Beyond rebinding, the default bindings will now map to whatever your keyboard layout is to offer a consistent out of the box experience. This means if you're using an AZERTY keyboard, we've got you covered, or DVORAK, or anything else.

A change like this can have some unexpected issues with configurations that we didn't get a chance to test out - please let us know if you experience an issue with the default bindings or with the rebinding process!

We haven't addressed Mouse usability yet - axis flipping, button remapping, scroll speeds, edge scroll - these are still on the list.

[h1]Year Length[/h1]
Another critical recent change was the doubling of the number of days per year for new games from 2 to 4. A great many Kontras out there felt that they were just getting to know their mortals when their time was up, so we decided to extend the year length to give you more time with them. This has the added benefit of giving your mortals additional time in their prime where they can do what they do best.

Allowing you to customize your experience is very important to us, so we've exposed this change as an option under the Game menu. You can set this to anywhere between 1 and 8 Days per Year out of the box - though there are already mods that push it further. The XP that your mortals gain will be scaled by the number of days per year to try to maintain a consistent leveling curve.

[h3]NOTE[/h3] Changing the number of days per year in a game will change the current year and the years of events that have transpired in your world. This is largely cosmetic as time is relative. In addition, you may experience certain events faster or slower depending on your year length.

[h1]Content Update 6: Tavern Decorations![/h1]

notes.title: Kingdom-Crier #2: The Hospitality Update Has Released!
notes.notes:
Greetings Kontras! Welcome to Kingdom-Crier #2! We're pleased to announce that the Hospitality Update has Released!

To Celebrate, Noble Fates is on sale for the next week!

[h1]The Hospitality Update[/h1]
[h3]Noble Fates Feature Update #1[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/59f6c1b27d2ee228e5ded2626c4802d99c44f83c.png[/img]

As you know, there are many wanderers who find themselves without a place to call home in the world of Noble Fates - they travel from kingdom to kingdom trying to survive and looking to secure that next meal. Some never get a chance to settle down before their time runs out.

These travelers can be a great source of new recruits, items, seeds, or even serve as your next meal. Now you can roll out the red carpet and show them just how great your kingdom really is. Guests will setup camp outside of your realm and it's up to you to offer them room and board for the night.

[h2]Run an Inn[/h2]
Offer beds, rooms, or entire buildings for rent. Meet expectations for a leg up on the recruiting process, exceed them for a chance to bypass it completely. Satisfy the needs of delegates to build your relationship with their Kingdom.

[h2]Build a Tavern[/h2]
Build a place where everyone can gather by a warm fire to eat and drink! Sell food and drink for an additional income stream. Leverage new decorations including the modular table to build a gathering place your kingdom can be proud of. Give them an experience they won't forget and they'll sing your praises as they travel the countryside with a full belly and a soothed mind.

[h2]Introducing Grapes and Wine![/h2]
Grow and harvest Grapes - eat 'em, cook 'em, turn 'em into Wine. Use the Winery to transform them into a quick fix for comfort. Use in moderation, however, as a drunk Noble may need to sleep it off.

[h2]Food and Drink Management[/h2]
Leverage the new Food and Drink Management tool to take control over the food your people can eat. Stop the Serfs from eating all of your Fine Meals and the Nobles from eating that Raw Imp you had plans for.

[h2]Lodging Need[/h2]
Address a need for lodging that scales with a Noble's Prestige. That Straw Bed in the corner might be enough for a fresh, unskilled recruit - but your most prestigious Nobles will need a nicely decorated Home of their own to be satisfied.

[h3]A Note About Saves[/h3]
This update is incompatible with saves from Noble Fates 0.23. You'll need to make a fresh run with this update. There is a new Beta branch on Steam named retired_0_23 which is compatible with your previous saves should you desire to continue with them.

notes.title: Kingdom-Crier #1: Announcing The Hospitality Update
notes.notes:
Greetings Kontras! Welcome to Kingdom-Crier #1 - the first in an ongoing series of bi-monthly community updates for Noble Fates.

These will serve as a place for you to keep your finger on the pulse of Noble Fates. We'll announce new major updates here, highlight the recent changes, and surface some of the cooler things happening in the community.

Without further ado...

[h1]Announcing The Hospitality Update[/h1]
[h3]Noble Fates Feature Update #1[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/c22c11f0304a1c3714ab565a2a67d674a5e6ccca.png[/img]

As you know, there are many wanderers who find themselves without a place to call home in the world of Noble Fates - they travel from kingdom to kingdom trying to survive and looking to secure that next meal. Some never get a chance to settle down before their time runs out.

These travelers can be a great source of new recruits, items, seeds, or even serve as your next meal. Now you can roll out the red carpet and show them just how great your kingdom really is. Guests will setup camp outside of your realm and it's up to you to offer them room and board for the night.

[h2]Run an Inn[/h2]
Offer beds, rooms, or entire buildings for rent. Meet expectations for a leg up on the recruiting process, exceed them for a chance to bypass it completely. Satisfy the needs of delegates to build your relationship with their Kingdom.

[h2]Build a Tavern[/h2]
Build a place where everyone can gather by a warm fire to eat and drink! Sell food and drink for an additional income stream. Leverage new decorations including the modular table to build a gathering place your kingdom can be proud of. Give them an experience they won't forget and they'll sing your praises as they travel the countryside with a full belly and a soothed mind.

[h2]Introducing Grapes and Wine![/h2]
Grow and harvest Grapes - eat 'em, cook 'em, turn 'em into Wine. Use the Winery to transform them into a quick fix for comfort. Use in moderation, however, as a drunk Noble may need to sleep it off.

[h2]Food and Drink Management[/h2]
Leverage the new Food and Drink Management tool to take control over the food your people can eat. Stop the Serfs from eating all of your Fine Meals and the Nobles from eating that Raw Imp you had plans for.

[h2]Lodging Need[/h2]
Address a need for lodging that scales with a Noble's Prestige. That Straw Bed in the corner might be enough for a fresh, unskilled recruit - but your most prestigious Nobles will need a nicely decorated Home of their own to be satisfied.

[h2]When Does it Release?[/h2]
The update will release in full on February 7th!

[h3]Experimental Branch[/h3]
We're happy to announce that the update is playable now in our new Experimental branch!

Participate in development and help us refine it before it launches. Keep in mind that this is a work in progress - there will be problems and additional features and content will come online as we prepare to release it - some of which may not make it into the Experimental branch. If you'd like to check it out, opt into the Experimental (or Experimental Development) branch using the Betas feature in Steam.

[h3]A Note About Saves[/h3]
This update is incompatible with saves from Noble Fates 0.23.*. We'll maintain an archive branch with the last 0.23.* build when it launches. You'll need to make a fresh run with this update.

[h1]What's new in Main?[/h1]
There have been a bevy of updates since the last summary, here are the highlights:

[code]Added Doorways/Arches to create soft breaks between indoor spaces or decorate interiors and exteriors!
Added Death Notifications and Cause of Death to the character sheet
Increased the frequency of young recruits
Added the ability to start a New Game from within the game, you no longer need to restart!
Streamlined and decreased refueling of lights
Improved mining yields and made them scale with character skill
Improved quality calculation for upper tier buildings including Wooden Roofs and Fine Wooden Walls[/code]
[h1]Community Content[/h1]
[i]PaddyMcfly used the new Columns to make some nice row houses[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/75728ea0cca644a82cf82aacb7a13043499b97ee.png[/img]

[i]Clown finished his Castle[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/2983c7a22413a98cc631f8538f18f41cc8d5204b.png[/img]

[i]Oskurd started a new series where he has to recruit anyone who wants to join[/i]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1z82gqhUCpU&list=PLdO4DqQovwqYlKHri_ji51qY5kvDSG-Bq
[h1]Content Mods[/h1]
[i]Narial dove in head first to develop [url=https://gitlab.com/u333/ledginstric/-/tree/main]Ledginstric[/url] - the most advanced Mod to date![/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/f6b1de9f6728ec518ea0859b9f1b01576fb1ef8b.png[/img]


Thanks for reading and thanks for playing!
The Noble Fates Team

notes.title: Happy One Month Anniversary!
notes.notes:
Hello Kontras! We can't believe it's been a month already!

Thank you so much for all of the support! We've seen over 20,000 players and more than 175,000 hours of Noble Fates played! Not bad for our scrappy little Kingdom Management Sim that no one knew about just 6 short weeks ago!

Today we released our 38th patch! Each of them has included hotfixes that have addressed Crashes, Performance Issues, and Balance as well as a bevy of QOL improvements. This patch also includes our 4th Content Update - adding the ability to place Wooden or Stone Columns to the previously released Wooden Hammer, Bronze Hammer, and Holiday Content updates.

Patch Notes:
[code]Noble Fates 0.23.0.70 (compatible with 0.22.*) released!
Hotfix Update #38 Content update #4

Add Columns!
    Buildable from structure menu
    Wood, Round Wood, and Stone available

Conflict
    Take opinion of ruler into account when deciding whether to offer an ultimatum about someone
    
Resources
    Double lifetime of Iron, Silver, and Copper when stored indoors
    Double lifetime of Stone indoors and outdoors
    
Crash Fixes
    Fix for crash when a farm is switched to No Plant Type
    Fix for crash when double clicking shelves when one is marked for move
    Fix for crash when marquee selecting a Mage
    Fix for crash when selecting things during Cinematic Moment
    Fix for crash related to examining x0 craft commands
    
Crafting
    Fix source of x0 remaining craft commands
    
Reactions
    Soften positive evil reactions to evil things
    
Fire Fighting
    Properly include certain terrain fires in fire fighting zone checks[/code]

We appreciate all of the feedback we've received along the way, and we think it's worth underscoring that we're listening. We've already improved the Intro, rebalanced Needs, improved Belonging distribution, balanced Resources, addressed Combat difficulty, and fixed Leveling progression based on your feedback! We'll continue to refine the game as we dig deeper into the next batch of improvements which include Key Rebinding, additional Difficulty Options, and the start of Customization.

In addition, the modding community has embraced the ease with which our game can be modded - there are a number of QOL Mods available on our Discord and the first Content Mods are starting to come online now.

This is only the beginning for Noble Fates. As discussed when we launched the Roadmap, we have strong plans for the future and are happy to announce that we are well underway on the first Feature Update. You can expect to hear more about that update very soon alongside the ability to try it out early in an Experimental Branch.

Thanks again for all of your support! Here's to a bright and prosperous future together!

Cheers!
The Noble Fates Team

notes.title: Happy Holidays from Noble Fates!
notes.notes:
Noble Fates is participating in the Steam Winter Sale!

To celebrate, we're releasing our second content update which includes Winter Holiday themed Seasonal Items! Check out the Holiday Tree, Holiday Wreath, or Santa Hat and bring a little bit of the Holiday cheer to your slice of Noberia!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/ba6363d9e3f396c00242a6cdc6ba29b44c3facd0.png[/img]

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]
Noble Fates 0.23.0.47 (compatible with 0.22.*) released![code]Hotfix Update #15 Content Update #2

Winter Holiday Seasonal Items
    Decorations (Decorations -> Seasonal)
        Holiday Tree
        Holiday Wreath
    Caps
        Santa Hat (Crafting Table)

Candelabra
    Reduce fuel burned per hour 
        
Performance
    Improve performance of the belongings screen when you have many items
    
Selection
    Improve selection behavior when there are items below the ground
[/code]
Restart the game (and steam if you don't see it) to pick it up!

[h2]Early Access Status[/h2]
This patch is the 15th(?!?!) patch we've released since Noble Fates launched just over a week ago. If you haven't played yet or are on the fence, there have been many excellent fixes in those patches!

Here are a few of the highlights:
[code]Numerous Crash Fixes and greatly improved stability

Intro
    Added the ability to reroll your starting group - get the group you want to play with!

Needs Rebalance
    Socialization, Comfort, and Ambition balance improved

Conversation Rebalance
    Conversations are now entirely optional, primarily for speeding up the recruiting process
    
Progression Rebalance
    Greatly increased the effect of work done on skill progression
    Greatly reduced the RNG aspect of leveling up       

Content
    Added Bronze Hammers and new Steel Hammer Art[/code]
[h2]The Roadmap[/h2]
In case you missed it, we also announced our Roadmap for Early Access. We've already addressed a number of the outstanding HotFixes and have started to work our way through the Content Updates. In addition, production is underway on the first Feature Update, which we'll be announcing next month!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1769420/view/5445412989034362287][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/7eef164027665e8f5418d4f40ecb8fee9fd8fc18.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Thank You![/h2]
For those of you who are playing, we hope you've enjoyed your time in Noberia! No doubt there have been a few bumps, but we think we've all done a great job of discussing and improving the game together! Though only a week into release, we feel that we've made great strides already, but this is only the beginning!

See [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1769420/view/5445412989034362287]the Roadmap[/url] for a clear picture of where we're heading and how we'll get there!

For those of you on the fence, we think we deliver an increasingly solid, replayable, and fresh take on the genre. There's no doubt there's more to do, but as massive fans of the genre, we think it's a great experience to have today! The Winter Sale (and break if you have one) is a great chance to check it out!

[h2]Happy Holidays[/h2]
The Noble Fates Team

notes.title: Noble Fates Roadmap
notes.notes:
[h1]Summer 2025 Update![/h1]
Let's take a moment to update the Roadmap and cross off a few boxes!

These days, there are 3 types of updates for Noble Fates - Hotfix Updates that address bugs and issues (including those that are listed on the Backlog and those that you Report in-game); Minor Updates that focus on reworking or expanding existing systems and filling them with additional content; and Feature Updates that add new features to the game expanding the overall breadth of what the game has to offer.

NOTE: We've replaced Content Updates with Minor Updates to better encompass the work that is being done to rework and expand on existing Systems during the march to 1.0.

[h2]Priority Progress[/h2]
[i]Progress against the Priority Fixes that we outlined in Fall 2024[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/2ea27e62ea3044ab8fb74e4b93da5904c484cc35.png[/img]
We launched the Conquest Update that included expansions to Diplomacy, a number of Strategic Options, Ballistas, Save Compatibility, and also improved Reachability detection. Then we tackled Hauling and Performance with targeted updates.

[h2]Notable Changes[/h2][code]60 Crash Fixes - bringing total to 310+!

[h2]Current Priorities[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/848a69c93667a25de5fac7f5df6be8ef003463ee.png[/img]
Some new entries here - including Fortress Mod support, Savable Mortal Presets, and allowing Buffs to exceed Skill Caps. We think these changes will better round out the whole experience as we head towards 1.0.

[h2]Feature Updates[/h2]
Finally, we have the Feature Updates. As a reminder, 8 of these will arrive during Early Access. 7 have landed so far. The most recent was Feature Update 7.

[i]Feature Update #7 - Noble Fates: Conquest![/i]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1769420/view/527588640879019600?l=english"][/dynamiclink]

Our biggest update to date, Noble Fates: Conquest greatly expanded on the mid to late game introducing the ability to Conquer your Island via Diplomacy or Warfare.

[h2]Feature Update #8 Status Update: In Progress[/h2]
The 8th Feature Update is in progress, and we're excited to share more details soon.

[h2]Early Access Status[/h2]
We're around 85% of the way through what we aim to accomplish with Early Access. Current estimates have us at 12 months or so from 1.0 with Major Update #8 landing somewhere in the middle.

We're in good shape for landing 1.0, due to your continued support. As always, you have our sincere gratitude!

[h2]Post 1.0 Plans[/h2]
We plan to support the game with a series of Hotfixes and Minor Updates that ensure the game is well balanced, performs well, and has consistent usability.

From there, the game could see subsequent Major Updates in one form or another depending on where things sit when the dust settles.

[h1]Original[/h1]
Cheers Kontras - we wanted to take a brief moment to loop you into our process and plans for Noble Fates.

To start, we think it’s important to call out the features that are present at launch. Everything present in the trailer is in the game, playable end-to-end and you can expect a solid 20-30 hours before replayability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/4ba86c64121ab7c483771c304d5c4be0d0ea7bbb.png[/img]

There are several kinds of updates we’re working on for Noble Fates:

First, we have Hotfixes - these contain bug, crash, quality of life, and balance fixes. You can expect anywhere from multiple of these per day (as we’ve been doing) to one every few weeks or so (once initial balance and bugs are sorted).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/e142938ded28043ff16a62c8de871aaeb333120f.png[/img]

Next, we have Content Updates - these will be new content for the existing systems. We’re already working on the first several of these, and plan to release them as soon as they’re ready. These will be piecemeal (Bronze Hammers, Wooden Hammers, Crossbows, etc.). You can expect these anywhere from once a week to one every few weeks. We’re also planning seasonal content and it will land as part of these.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/8de00af0b05b4f01aa4c73fb77e1c90fb0123871.png[/img]

Then, we have Feature Updates - these will introduce big new features - pulling the game in a new and exciting direction. These will be sizable enough that they’ll warrant a fresh, new playthrough of the game. These will be designated as bumps to the major version number of the game and are likely to break save compatibility. You can expect one of these every 6-8 weeks and expect them to be comparable in size and scope to the Breach/Carbuncle/Mage moment from the game (developed over 4-6 weeks before launch). These will be announced several weeks before they launch, and we’ll have an experimental branch where people can help us tune them before they go live. A minimum of 8 of these will be included in Early Access. Any that we don’t choose could still see the light of day as part of some future expansion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/79e87b86d18339a74ca8f1504ee361e3ec2b1e39.png[/img]

We’d like to maintain maximum agility with these - so we’ll choose the one that adds the most to the game at the beginning of each feature cycle. We aren’t committing to a specific set, but we are sharing the ones we’re excited about. We’d like to hear from you which ones you’d like and we’ll factor that into our process - even if they aren’t listed!

Finally, we have Steam Features - new high level features like Steam Workshop support and localization will be looped into the next feature update that is coming down the pipe when they are ready. 1.0 will have full Steam Workshop support, Localization, Achievements, Cloud Saves, and more.

To circle around, when we reach 1.0 (within 18 months), all Current Features, In-progress Hotfixes, Content Updates, a minimum of 8 Feature Updates, and Steam Features above will all be finished and included.

Everyone’s feedback has been fantastic so far. We’ll continue to listen, balance, fix, and adjust. Thanks so much for playing, and keep the feedback coming!

Thanks,
The Noble Fates Team

notes.title: Collaborative Storytelling
notes.notes:
Meet Diddle - they've just escaped The Marching Poems and there's a search party hot on their tail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/5b7ce77cfb70a83c4ad88b88916ff5824034c646.gif[/img]

In Noble Fates - you decide their fate and the world reacts.

Alignment, Opinions, and Relationships all factor into people's reactions. One of your people doesn't like Diddle because of something Diddle said and another because they just don't like Orcs. Someone else doesn't like the Marching Poems because they kicked a friend out 10 years ago. Each person weighs these factors when deciding their reaction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/781d2ec5546a3e2bff6a64455c2ba9726902f53d.gif[/img]

Maybe you decide to protect Diddle. Your people have mixed reactions and it costs you Goose. Diddle has good skills - so you think it was a decent trade - maybe even an upgrade. After a bit, the Marching Poems show up and you're presented with a chance to hand Diddle over. Some of the same people who weren't keen on you taking Diddle in want you to stand up for them now that you have. You decide to hold strong and war breaks out with the Marching Poems. There are still those who think that none of this was worth it, and they have a hard time letting it go.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/71927fe7b7a9534a1ea12993df0f3e54f4e8f1e9.gif[/img]

Perhaps you decide to capture Diddle instead. It turns out that Diddle is happy to have protection, even if they find themselves in chains. Similarly, when the Marching Poems arrive - you decide whether to hand them over or fight. This time some people in your kingdom react differently because you chose to capture Diddle first.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/095005d02f3cece2b3640cec16accb7c352a118b.gif[/img]

Of course - you could just execute Diddle, which the people (including the Marching Poems) will react to. The Marching Poems could thank you for doing their dirty work, and it could improve your relations.

Finally, you could do nothing - Diddle will go on their way without your help. Maybe the Marching Poems catch up to them somewhere else out there in the sim - but If they don't - Diddle will remember that you wronged them - and they'll do what they can to make sure you pay for it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/ff9b16b9a19e692f8ae4798ea18e2c0fb5a46408.gif[/img]

notes.title: Opinions, Alignment and Replayability
notes.notes:
In Noble Fates, the opinions and reactions of your Mortals can guide the day-to-day operations of each playthrough down a different path.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/3afebeb053b2b3e6e403d62467884bcd164d8b49.gif[/img]

Maybe the majority of your people are into Beans and you have a few with good Farming skills - so you move early on to establish Beans as your food source. You're growing them, harvesting them at the right time, and combining them with other ingredients into Meals.

Even though your people don't like Meat - maybe they prefer Leather and Hide gear - so you do a bit of Hunting, but then what do you do with all this Meat? Ah, the kingdom just over the hill really likes Venison - cool, we'll trade it to them because they'll give us a really good price for it - at least so long as we stay on friendly terms with them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/99530df5a4f84bd726404b043478f19e2697b057.png[/img]

Next time, maybe they don't like Hide or Leather either - so you skip straight to the Bronze Age and better Axes, or Hammers, or Swords!

Beyond this day-to-day nuance, there are critical, kingdom defining decisions that you'll face. Decisions that have negative consequences for someone. 

Mortals have a moral compass - Alignment - to help guide them in these decisions. It lands somewhere on a scale from Good to Evil. Generally speaking, it represents how much empathy a given Mortal has towards the victim in these interactions.

At the Good end, a Mortal stands up for the victim, even if they don't like them - at least... Well, as long as they don't hate them. At the Evil end, they're more likely to side a bit with the aggressor, but really they mostly care about themselves. In the middle, we have Neutrals, they support their friends, regardless of morality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/272c15747db5cc2e9f054a25473b16ef05ca027d.png[/img]

Ok - so we have this survivor from the raid that just came through - and I mean, they are the enemy - but really they're just doing their job. So you have a few Good people who would prefer it if you tend their wounds and let them go. Then you've got a few indifferent Neutrals who are with you if you want to imprison them and force them into a life of hard labor. And then you've got Tom over in the corner thinking their skin would make a nice, new pair of boots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41584603/19f111700b2ed66d162ba15908bcd363d308c469.png[/img]

Stepping back this mean that each playthrough can be pretty different. It's likely that you'll discover just what type of Kingdom you're running along the way - and that your place in your world's overarching story will be different each time. It'll change further as your Kingdom changes - with the other kingdoms reacting and evolving right along with you.

That's Noble Fates.
